title: Bond Line Formula Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A metro map shows a city in a few lines, a stick figure shows a person in five strokes, and a chemist draws a big molecule as one zigzag. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we learn the structural representations of organic compounds.

On the molecule bench, butane is drawn as a complete structural formula bond by bond, squeezed into the condensed formula CH3CH2CH2CH3, then turned into a bond line zigzag. We learn the bond line rules (corners and ends are carbons, hidden hydrogens, written heteroatoms, rings as shapes), read a branched drawing link by link to get C5H12, and show depth with wedge and dash. Then a full worked example, the exam trap, an original JEE / NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 79 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three drawings, one idea
0:33 Complete, condensed and bond line
1:09 The molecule bench: butane three ways
1:49 Rules of bond line drawings and rings
2:17 Read a bond line drawing, link by link
2:47 Wedge and dash: drawing in 3D
3:30 Worked example: bond line to formula
4:19 Exam trap: counting carbons in a zigzag
4:45 Practice question (JEE / NEET pattern)
5:28 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Classification of Organic Compounds. Why do chemists sort millions of carbon compounds into families?

Video by Quest Academy.
